$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. `checked` is proved against this repository by
tests/test_manifest.py in this repository's own CI; `declared` is a statement
nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
THE DISTRIBUTION IS NOT CALLED WHAT ANYTHING ELSE HERE IS CALLED. The
repository is `engram`, the import is `engram`, and the thing you `pip
install` is `engdbram`. CHANGELOG records the rename from `engram-ai`
because the plain name was taken. Three names for one component is the sort
of fact that costs somebody an afternoon, and it is checked against
pyproject rather than restated.
THREE CONSOLE SCRIPTS, AND estate.json DECLARES ONE. That is correct rather
than an omission: `engram-mcp` is what the deployments spawn, and the other
two are a CLI a person runs and a benchmark harness. The registry records
what a deployment installs and this records what the package installs, and
the difference between the two lists is exactly the information neither file
holds alone.
`[project.scripts]` IS ALREADY A CROSS-REPOSITORY CONTRACT. stack-k8s's
console.Dockerfile installs the Python tools by reading it and says so in a
comment; stack-up's `install_py_tool engram engram-mcp "[mcp]"` names the
script and the extra. A script added here without a manifest entry is a
component the console image would install and nothing would have declared.
WHAT COULD NOT BE RUN HERE, SAID PLAINLY. This repository has no virtualenv
on the machine this was written on, its suite pulls fastembed and that
downloads ONNX models, and the system interpreter is EXTERNALLY-MANAGED.
Nothing was installed to work around that. So the parsing half of the test
was run against a sibling repository's pytest, and the half that invokes the
console scripts SKIPS when the package is not importable and runs in this
repository's own CI, where it is.

it_is_spawned_not_served.why: An MCP server over stdio: no network listener and no port to guard, which is why no launcher polls it and why this declares no health path. The console spawns it as a child process.

the_mcp_extra_is_how_it_is_installed.why: stack-up runs `install_py_tool engram engram-mcp "[mcp]" mcp`. The extra is not in [project.scripts] and cannot be checked from it, so it is declared.

no_deployment_installs_it.why: The command somebody uses against their own store. Not in estate.json's `runs` because nothing schedules or supervises it.

nothing_should_install_it.why: The benchmark harness, in the sense trailryx's seven dev-tools are: its absence from every deployment is the answer rather than a question.
